response.sql: WITH color_counts AS (SELECT p.product_color, COUNT(ili.product_id) AS line_item_count FROM Products AS p LEFT JOIN Invoice_Line_Items AS ili ON ili.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.product_color), color_metrics AS (SELECT line_item_count, AVG(line_item_count) OVER () AS average_count_per_color, SUM(line_item_count) OVER () AS total_line_items FROM color_counts) SELECT AVG(line_item_count) AS average_count, AVG(line_item_count * 1.0 / NULLIF(total_line_items, 0)) AS average_share, AVG(line_item_count - average_count_per_color) AS average_excess_count FROM color_metrics WHERE line_item_count > average_count_per_color;

assumptions.assumption: Every color in Products participates in the per-color average, including colors with zero invoice line items. NULL is one color group.

alternatives.interpretation: Calculate the per-color average using only colors represented by invoice line items.
alternatives.sql: WITH color_counts AS (SELECT p.product_color, COUNT(*) AS line_item_count FROM Invoice_Line_Items AS ili JOIN Products AS p ON p.product_id = ili.product_id GROUP BY p.product_color), color_metrics AS (SELECT line_item_count, AVG(line_item_count) OVER () AS average_count_per_color, SUM(line_item_count) OVER () AS total_line_items FROM color_counts) SELECT AVG(line_item_count) AS average_count, AVG(line_item_count * 1.0 / NULLIF(total_line_items, 0)) AS average_share, AVG(line_item_count - average_count_per_color) AS average_excess_count FROM color_metrics WHERE line_item_count > average_count_per_color;
